# PandasWise

> PandasWise is a free, original educational website about giant pandas (Ailuropoda melanoleuca) and red pandas (Ailurus). It explains panda biology, diet, behavior, habitat, conservation status and how the two species differ, and keeps a verified, country by country list of zoos and reserves where giant pandas and red pandas can be seen, each entry checked against an official page with a last verified date. 
Content is general education written from cited sources (IUCN, WWF, Smithsonian's National Zoo, San Diego Zoo Wildlife Alliance, peer reviewed studies and official zoo announcements). Zoo details change; check with the zoo before visiting.

## Guides
- [Giant panda facts](https://pandaswise.com/giant-panda.html): Giant panda facts in one place: scientific name, size and weight, the pseudo thumb, how cubs grow, lifespan, wild population and IUCN status, with sources.
- [Red panda facts](https://pandaswise.com/red-panda.html): Red panda facts: why it is not a bear or a raccoon, the two species debate, size, bamboo diet, life in the trees, cubs, lifespan and Endangered status.
- [Panda diet: what pandas eat](https://pandaswise.com/diet.html): What giant pandas and red pandas eat, how much bamboo they need each day, why bamboo barely feeds them, what else they eat, and what zoos feed them.
- [Panda behavior](https://pandaswise.com/behavior.html): How giant and red pandas behave: daily routine, sleep, solitary life, scent marking, vocal sounds, climbing, mating season and raising cubs.
- [Panda habitat and range](https://pandaswise.com/habitat.html): Where giant pandas and red pandas live in the wild: mountain ranges, countries, elevations, forest types and the Giant Panda National Park.
- [Panda conservation](https://pandaswise.com/conservation.html): Giant and red panda conservation explained: IUCN status history, latest population numbers, the main threats, what has worked and how to help.
- [Giant panda vs red panda comparison](https://pandaswise.com/giant-vs-red-panda.html): Giant panda vs red panda compared side by side: family, size, weight, diet, range, behavior, cubs, lifespan and IUCN status, plus what they have in common.
- [Panda FAQ: myths vs facts](https://pandaswise.com/faq.html): Panda myths and facts answered with sources: are pandas lazy, bad at breeding, raccoons, endangered, dangerous or only in China? Clear, sourced answers.
- [Panda glossary](https://pandaswise.com/glossary.html): Panda glossary: pseudo thumb, Ailuridae, delayed implantation, crepuscular and other giant and red panda terms, each explained in plain English.

## Tools
- [Where to see pandas: verified zoo list](https://pandaswise.com/where-to-see-pandas.html): Zoos and reserves with giant pandas and red pandas, country by country, each checked against the zoo's own official page on 12 October 2026.
- [Panda games](https://pandaswise.com/games/): Free original panda games for kids and adults: catch bamboo with a hungry giant panda, or sort facts into giant or red panda. Every round ends with a fact.
- [Bamboo Breakfast](https://pandaswise.com/games/bamboo-breakfast/): Bamboo Breakfast is a free giant panda game: catch falling bamboo for 30 seconds and learn sourced facts about how much bamboo pandas really eat.
- [Which Panda Is It?](https://pandaswise.com/games/which-panda-is-it/): A free sorting game: read a fact and decide whether it describes the giant panda, the red panda, or both. Ten rounds, each with a sourced explanation.
- [Panda resources for teachers](https://pandaswise.com/teachers/): Free panda resources for teachers: lesson ideas by grade band linked to NGSS life science standards, a printable quiz with answers, vocabulary and games.
- [For students and researchers](https://pandaswise.com/researchers/): Key peer reviewed papers behind PandasWise articles on giant and red pandas, with full citations and DOIs: energy, coat colour, species and bamboo.
  - Sections: [Giant pandas by country](https://pandaswise.com/where-to-see-pandas.html#outside-china), [Giant pandas in China](https://pandaswise.com/where-to-see-pandas.html#china), [Red pandas by country](https://pandaswise.com/where-to-see-pandas.html#red-pandas), [Countries with no giant pandas now](https://pandaswise.com/where-to-see-pandas.html#none-now)

## Blog
- [Are giant pandas still endangered?](https://pandaswise.com/blog/are-giant-pandas-still-endangered.html): No: the IUCN has listed giant pandas as Vulnerable since 2016. What that means, the latest wild population figures and what still threatens them.
- [Are red pandas nocturnal?](https://pandaswise.com/blog/are-red-pandas-nocturnal.html): Red pandas are not strictly nocturnal. They are mostly crepuscular, busiest at dawn and dusk, and awake about 45% of the day. What studies show.
- [Are red pandas related to giant pandas?](https://pandaswise.com/blog/are-red-pandas-related-to-giant-pandas.html): Red and giant pandas are only distant relatives: one is a bear, the other the last of its own family. What DNA shows, and why both have a false thumb.
- [Do pandas have thumbs?](https://pandaswise.com/blog/do-pandas-have-thumbs.html): Giant pandas have a false thumb: an enlarged wrist bone that grips bamboo. How it works, how old it is, and why red pandas have one too.
- [Do pandas hibernate?](https://pandaswise.com/blog/do-pandas-hibernate.html): Giant pandas do not hibernate: a bamboo diet cannot build the fat reserves it needs. How they cope with winter, and how red pandas save energy.
- [How big is a red panda's home range?](https://pandaswise.com/blog/how-big-is-a-red-panda-home-range.html): GPS collars put the median red panda home range at about 1.4 square km. Males use more space than females, and roads and forest loss change how they roam.
- [How do giant pandas communicate?](https://pandaswise.com/blog/how-do-giant-pandas-communicate.html): Giant pandas live mostly alone, so they talk through scent marks and calls. How handstand marking, scent and bleats carry messages, with the research.
- [How do red pandas stay warm?](https://pandaswise.com/blog/how-do-red-pandas-stay-warm.html): Red pandas stay warm with dense fur, furry soles and a bushy tail, by curling into a ball and by burning more energy in winter. What studies show.
- [How long do pandas live?](https://pandaswise.com/blog/how-long-do-pandas-live.html): Giant pandas live about 15 to 20 years in the wild and around 30 in zoos; the record is 38. Red pandas can reach 23. What limits a panda's lifespan.
- [How long is a giant panda pregnancy?](https://pandaswise.com/blog/how-long-is-a-giant-panda-pregnancy.html): Giant panda pregnancy lasts about 90 to 180 days, but after delayed implantation the fetus grows for only about 42 days. What hormone studies show.
- [How much bamboo does a giant panda eat a day?](https://pandaswise.com/blog/how-much-bamboo-does-a-panda-eat.html): A giant panda eats roughly 12 to 45 kg of bamboo a day. Why sources disagree, how shoots vs leaves change the number, and how red pandas compare.
- [How much do giant pandas sleep?](https://pandaswise.com/blog/how-much-do-giant-pandas-sleep.html): Giant pandas eat for 10 to 16 hours a day and sleep most of the rest, in naps of 2 to 4 hours. What GPS collar studies reveal about when pandas rest.
- [How strong is a giant panda's bite?](https://pandaswise.com/blog/how-strong-is-a-giant-panda-bite.html): Giant pandas have one of the strongest bites of any bear for their size. How their skull, jaw muscles and molars crush bamboo, with the research behind it.
- [What do red pandas eat?](https://pandaswise.com/blog/what-do-red-pandas-eat.html): Red pandas eat mostly bamboo leaf tips and shoots, plus some fruit, roots, insects and the odd egg. What field and genetic studies show about their diet.
- [Why are baby pandas so small?](https://pandaswise.com/blog/why-are-baby-pandas-so-small.html): A newborn giant panda weighs about 3 to 5 ounces, roughly 1/900th of its mother. Skeletal scans suggest a short gestation after implantation explains why.
- [Why are giant pandas black and white?](https://pandaswise.com/blog/why-are-pandas-black-and-white.html): Why giant pandas are black and white: the leading study points to snow and shade camouflage for the body and signalling for the ears and eye patches.
- [Why are red pandas endangered?](https://pandaswise.com/blog/why-are-red-pandas-endangered.html): Red pandas are Endangered because their mountain forests are cut, grazed and split by roads, and because they are trapped and poached. What studies show.
- [Why are red pandas red?](https://pandaswise.com/blog/why-are-red-pandas-red.html): Red pandas are red because the russet coat blends with reddish brown moss and white lichen in their forest canopy. How the coat, mask, belly and tail work.
- [Why do giant pandas eat bamboo if they are carnivores?](https://pandaswise.com/blog/why-do-pandas-eat-bamboo-if-they-are-carnivores.html): Giant pandas belong to the order Carnivora yet live on bamboo. What genome, taste gene, gut microbe and energy studies reveal about this unusual diet.
